items.text: According to CBS, Democrats reached at least 54 Senate seats (with many seats flipping, including Texas, Ohio, Maine and North Carolina) and also won the House. Hakeem Jeffries will become the first Black Speaker of the House. Trump accepted the result but said he may veto legislation, which in practice means two years of divided government.
items.title: Democrats take Congress

items.text: In Qatar-brokered talks, Iran called the US reply to its terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz insufficient. Trump confirmed Tuesday's limited strike; US media report plans for broader post-election strikes. The direction of oil prices hinges on this.
items.title: Iran–US: Hormuz still closed

items.text: Brent is down about 16% so far this week; defense (Lockheed -7%) and energy stocks were the biggest losers. With oil the main driver of inflation this year, the move also shifts Fed and ECB expectations.
items.title: Oil slump, energy stocks lag

items.text: Euro-area inflation rose to 4.0% in October; Bundesbank President Nagel said a December hike will probably be needed. Helped by this and a weaker dollar, the euro is at its strongest since early October.
items.title: Rate-hike signal in Europe

items.text: CVS announced a plan to split in two; Microsoft rose 7% and McDonald's about 6%. Goldman said Democratic gains in the states make data-center moratoriums more likely, which could affect about 45% of planned capacity; CoreWeave fell 10%.
items.title: Corporate news
